eval_feedback: eval 5 #3 is self-contradictory as written and is this run's biggest grading hazard. Its first clause requires that gaps appear only as square-bracketed placeholders inside the draft article AND ITS TABLE, yet it cites failure-ledger F13, whose family 2 (references/anti-slop-ruleset.md §6) makes any [CLIENT DATA / [SOURCE NEEDED inside paste-ready copy FAIL-grade and explicitly protects customer-voice hedging. A published comparison table cannot satisfy both. The prior baseline hit the same fork and logged it as a judgment call. Proposed rewording: gaps appear either as square-bracketed placeholders in draft-only sections or as customer-voice absence statements in publishable copy, and an agency-to-client aside such as 'data needed from client' fails in both.

eval 2 #6's clause 'every medical term explained in plain words on first use' needs a materiality rule or an enumerated term list. «συστολική» and «περιχειρίδα» clearly qualify; «δύσπνοια» and «θωρακικό πόνο» are contestable, and a whole expectation's verdict currently turns on that contest.

eval 1 #4 and eval 3 #1 both exempt self-scores, character/word-count annotations and quoted skill thresholds, but say nothing about ADVICE PARAMETERS — «3–4 εβδομάδες πριν», 'set terms to 14 days', 'eight to thirteen weeks'. These are recommendations rather than measurements, yet they are numerals inside a no-invented-numbers eval. The prior baseline's backlog already carries 'e3#1 advice-parameter clause' and it is still open.

eval 1 #1 requires the provider's full supplied name inside the first 150 BODY words. For a first-person service page that is a real constraint but an invisible one: nothing in the prompt or the brief signals that the legal entity must appear in the page copy rather than in the deliverable header. Either the prompt should ask for it, or the expectation should accept the name anywhere in the draft page.

eval 4 #3's blocking-language clause is the only place in the suite that tests the skill's own step-9 publish gate, and it is easy to fail by writing a helpful 'ship it now' recommendation. Worth stating in the eval PROMPT that the publish / do-not-publish call is part of the deliverable, so the failure measures judgement rather than prompt-reading.

No eval in this suite tests compliance with the brief's own word-count target. Both English drafts overran by more than 20% and nothing caught it; the honest self-scores were volunteered, not required. A structure expectation with a plus-or-minus 15% band would close the gap.

run_integrity.f8_class_event: BOTH of this run's primary inputs mutated mid-run. (1) references/anti-slop-ruleset.md — a named grading input — was read at its committed 239-line state at run start and is 257 lines in the working tree by the end, a parallel agent having added a new FAIL-grade §6 family 7 (connector placeholders `~~category` on client-read surfaces, greppable `~~`) plus a recurrence note and the new token `δεξιότητ` on the English-artefact-names advisory. (2) The target SKILL.md itself was bumped 4.2.4 -> 4.2.5, adding a Data-Sources paragraph requiring `~~` resolution and rewriting the Output Validation source-label line that previously read '(~~SEO tool data, user-provided, or estimated)'. This is the ledger F8 signature — review target mutated during an in-flight review — in its Mode B form; the F14 second-mechanism residual (parallel agents writing shared files while another actor is working) is the mechanism.
run_integrity.impact_on_verdicts: NONE, verified rather than assumed. Scripted scan of all five deliverables and all three raw-Greek files returns 0 occurrences of `~~` and 0 of `δεξιότητ`. All five deliverables independently label provenance in plain language — «**Πηγή δεδομένων:** αποκλειστικά το brief της 2026-08-03», «**Πηγή δεδομένων:** αποκλειστικά το brief του ιατρείου», 'Data provenance: everything in the draft is either (a) reasoning the reader can verify …', 'SEO tooling | None connected' — i.e. they already satisfy 4.2.5's family-7 rule without having seen it. No verdict in this file would change under the newer texts; every §6 verdict was graded against the HEAD 239-line text, which is the version the executor had loaded, and that is stated so the record is reconstructible.
run_integrity.recommendation: No re-grade needed, but the near miss is the finding. Mode B should declare a frozen input manifest at launch the way Mode A declares a frozen target (F8 guard): a skill's SKILL.md and references are simultaneously the executor's instructions and the grader's rubric, so a mid-run edit can silently change what 'correct' means. Had my outputs contained a single `~~` token, this run would have produced a verdict against a rule that did not exist when the output was written.
